what_this_lane_repairs.defect: A spread pick could not be graded at all. classifyMarketFamilyForGrading('spread') returned family 'unsupported', so every spread submitted through the Smart Form was skipped by name before any result was consulted.
what_this_lane_repairs.why_it_is_not_merely_a_missing_case: A spread is not an over/under. inferSelectionSide('Chiefs -2.5') returns null, so the generic over/under branch the grading loop falls through to cannot express a spread even if the family were admitted — it would skip on selection_side_unknown instead. The family needed its own outcome derivation, not an entry in a table.
what_this_lane_repairs.production_relevance_measured: 2 of the 4 picks in the governed cohort (metadata ? 'distributionMode') are spreads: 29da425a 'Broncos +3' line +3.00 and 04174f12 'Chiefs -2.5' line -2.50, both status=validated, both capper_id griff843. Their persisted line sign is exactly the convention this repair assumes — signed from the selected participant's perspective — so cover margin is actual_value + line and the three-branch win/loss/push split is the correct reading of a zero cover.

production_measurement.what_this_establishes: The market-key guard is load-bearing rather than defensive. There are 1,849 '%-sp' rows in production and every one of them carries participant_id NULL — an unattributed raw score with no side. The candidate lookup can reach them. Grading a spread off one would invent a side that was never attested. Refusing any key but game_spread_margin by name is what prevents that, and it is why this lane skips rather than interprets.
production_measurement.and_what_it_does_not: There are zero game_spread_margin rows anywhere, so no production or staging spread can actually settle today. That is the same results-supply constraint (layer 3) that already blocks moneyline, and this lane does not claim to move it.

coverage_gap.status: OPEN, and stated rather than papered over
coverage_gap.finding: No staging test exercises game_spread_margin. This lane's new behaviour is proven statically (92/92) and is not proven against a real database.
why_it_could_not_be_closed_inside_this_l: file_scope_lock is pinned at lane-start and admits exactly two paths — apps/api/src/grading-service.ts and apps/api/src/grading-service.test.ts. A new *.test.ts proof file is not declarable here, and an agent cannot widen the lock.
Wiring any new test file into the t1-proof:live battery requires editing root package.json, which is also outside this lock.

There are zero game_spread_margin rows in production and none in staging, so there is no existing row to grade against; a staging proof would have to seed its own, which is exactly the shape of test this lock forbids.
coverage_gap.why_it_is_not_a_reason_to_hold_the_lane: The refusal side of the change — the market-key guard — is the side that can cause harm, and it is the side that fails closed: an unrecognised key skips by name. The acceptance side cannot fire in any environment today because no game_spread_margin row exists. So the staging gap is a gap in proving a path that is currently unreachable, not a gap in proving a path that is running.
coverage_gap.disposition: Recorded as a dependency for the follow-on lane that supplies game_spread_margin results. That lane owns the staging proof, because it is the lane that creates the row the proof needs.
